solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fancy dumping diet? It's the right moment!

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters that follow get a free rearrangement

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandoning a diet decides now is the moment to indulge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at dessert, and the answer is indeed about puddings, which makes the anagram apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding time is an old idiom for the opportune or critical moment, originally the start of dinner when pudding was served first.

clue.text: Winds up on river, thus beginning of nice time with nothing to do

parts.note: winds up means brings to an end
Ea is a dictionary word for a river or watercourse
so means in this way

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of nice

explanation.surface: Someone finishing up by a river and enjoying the start of an idle spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Ea is an old dictionary word for a river or stream, little seen outside crosswords; 'on' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The close season is the part of the year when hunting or fishing is banned, or a sport is not played, so there is nothing to do.

clue.text: Herald: animal time and again escaping

indicators.note: whatever is escaping gets out and away, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: critter is an informal word for a creature
T for time, and again T, a second one

explanation.surface: A herald's animal keeps running off.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ts leave CRITTER, which is what the 'and again' asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was an official who announced news in public, a herald in the literal sense.

clue.text: Spymaster enters into crippling punishment

indicators.note: something that enters into another goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: laming means disabling or crippling
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief takes part in a brutal punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes in the middle of LAMING: LAM(M)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is to thrash, so a lamming is a beating given as punishment.

clue.text: Regret very good bishop overlooking one Head

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
Right Reverend, the title of a bishop, abbreviated Rt Rev or RR
Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Remorse over a saintly bishop who looks down on a single head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overlooking' puts the bishop's letters above the rest. A ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Fife Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorriness is the state of being sorry, which is regret.

clue.text: Source of power needing to work out of centre

indicators.note: letters put to work are set to a new task, here a new order
with the centre taken out, the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A power source that needs fixing, away from the middle of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The central D of NEEDING goes, and the remaining six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a machine that converts fuel into motion, the power plant of a vehicle.

clue.text: Reports from parts of Germany

definitions.meaning: first meaning: declares or says formally
second meaning: the federal divisions of the country, the Länder

explanation.surface: News dispatches coming out of German regions.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to declare formally, and Germany is a federation made up of sixteen states.

clue.text: One hour at home got across mum's spirit

indicators.note: a word that has got across another stretches over it, enclosing it

parts.note: a means one
standard abbreviation
in means at home
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone home for an hour discovers their mother's ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after mum is just a link, read as 'is'; 'spirit' looks like a ghost but is a named evil being.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahriman is the evil spirit, the destructive power opposed to the good god in Zoroastrian belief.

clue.text: Ancient settlement found once after heading for Scotland?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: first letter of Scotland

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and cast it, so the letters are melted down and recast

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a former settlement after setting out for Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like a past tense meaning discovered, but it is the anagram signal; the S is placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Scone, near Perth, was the ancient royal centre where Scottish kings were crowned on the Stone of Scone.

clue.text: Exclamations of surprise after salmon beheaded

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: cohos are Pacific salmon, the plural of coho

explanation.surface: People exclaim in shock at the sight of decapitated fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The coho, or silver salmon, is a North Pacific species; drop its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Oho is an interjection expressing surprise or triumph, so ohos are such exclamations.

clue.text: Row at university about mineral found on borders of lake

definitions.text: mineral found on borders of lake

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: to row is to use an oar

explanation.surface: A university rowing crew turns its attention to minerals by a lake shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row at university' puts U before the turned OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Urao is a natural sodium carbonate mineral deposited around the edges of soda lakes, notably in Venezuela.

clue.text: Quiet old female in the soup!

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
chi is an old word for a girl or woman, from Romany

explanation.surface: A quiet old woman is in trouble, in the soup!
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is the idiom for in trouble, a misleading frame for a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shchi is a Russian cabbage soup.

clue.text: Provide example of present upset involving Italy

indicators.note: involving means wrapping something up inside, so one letter goes within

parts.note: the instant is the present moment
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
ate, as in what's eating you, means troubled or upset

explanation.surface: Someone illustrates a point about an upsetting gift that involves Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift, but it is the present moment, and 'upset' is a past tense, as in what ate him.
explanation.definitionFit: To instantiate is to represent by an instance, to give a concrete example of something abstract.

clue.text: Maître seen in director's compound

indicators.note: a thing seen in another is inside it, so it goes into the middle

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Me is the French abbreviation for Maître, the title of a lawyer

explanation.surface: A French lawyer is spotted at a director's walled residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like a walled estate, but here it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimer is a chemical compound made of two identical molecules joined together.

clue.text: Talk at length about a drawer with decorative edging

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase's letters go round the rest

parts.note: to go on is to talk at length
taken as written
DR is the abbreviation for drawer, as on a cheque

explanation.surface: Someone drones on about a chest of drawers with an ornate trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture, but it is the person who draws a cheque, abbreviated on banking forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadroon is a decorative moulding of fluting or reeding, often found on the edges of silverware and furniture.

clue.text: French reputed to be holding back army unit in desert as before

indicators.note: a word holding another has it inside, enclosing it

parts.note: dit is French for said or reputed

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the unit is read in reverse

parts.note: the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A French army unit stationed out in the desert, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is not the sandy place but the noun for what one deserves, as in just deserts; 'as before' marks an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerit once meant merit or desert, what one has earned, before it came to mean a fault.

clue.text: Chaps going about a search for excavated burial-places

indicators.note: going about something means going round it, so these letters surround the rest

parts.note: cats is jazz slang for men, chaps
taken as written
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: Men out hunting for the underground tombs where the dead lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats for chaps is old jazz slang, as in hep cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground cemeteries cut into rock, such as those beneath Rome.

clue.text: Feature stuff on catkin

parts.note: to line is to stuff or fill, as in lining one's pockets
an ament is a catkin

explanation.surface: A distinctive characteristic of material on a willow's catkin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature or characteristic, especially of the face.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon by no means including a bit of nitrogen

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: none as an adverb means not at all
taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small part of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of nitrogen, also its chemical symbol

explanation.surface: A hydrocarbon that by no means contains even a little nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N go into NONE: NON(AN)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonane is an alkane with nine carbon atoms, a hydrocarbon found in petroleum.

clue.text: Charlie in rock against getting excited in one of his pieces?

definitions.text: excited in one of his pieces?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: aa is rough, clinkery lava rock
a charlie is a fool, as is a git
to can mean against, as in face to face

explanation.surface: A rock musician called Charlie gets worked up in one of his songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie in rock' suggests a rock star such as the Rolling Stones' Charlie Watts, whose pieces might be marked thus; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning to be played in an agitated, excited manner.

clue.text: Part of poem and German dance in S Africa

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
Tanz is the German word for dance

explanation.surface: A poem's verse is set alongside a German dance performed in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The German word for dance must be known; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Lacking a drink before party? Impossible!

parts.note: no can means without a can of drink
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Going to a party without a drink is out of the question.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal meaning it cannot be done.

clue.text: Soldier Pike arresting German made a performance

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: arresting someone means holding them, so one letter is held inside

parts.note: ged is a northern and Scots word for the pike fish
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A soldier named Pike arrests a German and makes a show of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pike' poses as a soldier's surname, or a weapon; it is the fish, under its northern dialect name.
explanation.definitionFit: To gig is to play a gig, a live musical engagement, so gigged means gave a performance.

clue.text: Delegate's place accepted by comic Jack

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the word goes inside the other

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian
to place is to put

explanation.surface: A comedian approves of a delegate's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delegate's' is the verb plus a link 's, read as 'delegate is'; Jack Dee is a deadpan British stand-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To depute is to appoint someone to act on your behalf, to delegate.

clue.text: A number caught in Geneva with hard substance

indicators.note: something caught in another is trapped inside it

parts.note: geneva is an old name for gin, from the Dutch genever
taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Several people are arrested in a Swiss city with something solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Geneva' sends the solver to Switzerland; it is the Dutch-style gin also called genever.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganoin is the hard, shiny, enamel-like substance that coats the scales of certain fish.

clue.text: Pleasant spot close to Epping Forest

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: last letter of Epping
the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A nice place near Epping Forest, the woodland on London's north-eastern edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near; it is the last-letter signal, and 'Forest' is a different forest from Epping.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a cultivated plot, the archetypal pleasant spot.

clue.text: Oireachtas not right to upset leader of republic

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over and disorder, so the letters are scrambled
not right means without the abbreviation for right, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: taken as written; the Oireachtas is the Irish parliament
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The Irish parliament, left-leaning, sets out to unseat the head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Irish politics on both sides: the Oireachtas is the parliament of the Republic of Ireland, and the answer is its prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the prime minister and head of government of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Flower with neat edge

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, an ox
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: A flower with a tidy border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old noun for cattle, as in neat's-foot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a woodland flower of the primrose family, like a cowslip.

clue.text: Heads dropping, notice trap in alloy

indicators.note: with heads dropped, each word loses its first letter

parts.note: to spot is to notice
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Drooping heads spot a trap made of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes from SPOT and G from GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Potin is an old alloy of copper, zinc, lead and tin, used for Celtic coins.

clue.text: Course around lake is excellent in Scotland

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so these letters go round the other

parts.note: a way is a route or course
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A route round a loch is fine, as the Scots say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots word is best known from the folk song O Waly, Waly.
explanation.definitionFit: Waly is a Scots adjective meaning fine, excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Temple vestibules for Iona conceivably

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: conceivably means as it might possibly be, so the letters take another possible arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Entrances to temples, possibly fitting for the holy island of Iona.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is the Hebridean island famous for its abbey, a natural place for temple talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronaoi is the plural of pronaos, the porch or vestibule in front of the cella of a Greek temple.

clue.text: Novelist, male American hit endlessly with abuse

indicators.note: with no end, the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation
to lam is to hit or thrash
mud is slander or abuse, as in mud-slinging

explanation.surface: A male American novelist is attacked with endless abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading 'hit' as a bestseller; it is the verb, cut short to LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Malamud was an American novelist, author of The Natural and The Fixer.

clue.text: Ray is worker keeping mum? The opposite

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
the opposite swaps which holds which, so the keeper becomes the one kept within

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is a worker who keeps quiet about something, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping mum' looks like the idiom for staying silent; 'The opposite' reverses who holds whom, so the mother holds the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A manta is a very large ray, a flat fish with wing-like fins.

clue.text: Pick little after end of hurricane

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: last letter of hurricane
lite is a variant spelling of light in the sense of slight or little

explanation.surface: Choose something small once the hurricane has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick little' reads as one instruction, but Pick is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its best members, the elite.

clue.text: Opening a block in Edinburgh

parts.note: taken as written
dit is a Scots word meaning to block or stop up

explanation.surface: A gap in a block of buildings in Scotland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Edinburgh' flags a Scots word rather than a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal opening or passage into a mine.

clue.text: BP not in order supply one tiny shop

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, supply means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new shape

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The oil company BP fails to stock even a single small shop.
explanation.walkthrough: BP looks like the oil company; it is blood pressure, and 'supply' is the adverb from supple, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypotension is abnormally low blood pressure, a reading out of the normal range.
